impasto-oil.name: Palette-knife impasto oil
impasto-oil.still: Impasto oil painting laid with a palette knife, in a hot three-strip-era palette. A sunset glow burns from wine through red and orange to gold across roughly half the frame; red-brown takes about a quarter, and large warm near-black silhouettes the rest. Long horizontal knife slabs band the brightest open areas, shorter strokes follow form elsewhere, with calm thin areas between; ridges lit from upper left, paint thickest in the highlights, linen weave showing where thin. Strong backlight with gold rims. Epic-poster composition: big dark shapes set low against the glowing light, the focal form kept a readable warm mid-tone, never a silhouette. Avoid: same-size tiled strokes, muddy browns, smooth gradients.
impasto-oil.shot: A slow truck and push across the wide while the light drops to a raking angle so every knife ridge catches it, then settles. The next image is laid over this one in a sweeping paint-over of fresh knife strokes, never a dissolve.
impasto-oil.sound: A lush, sweeping 1930s string orchestra at a slow, broad tempo, with French horns, harp arpeggios and the warm grain of an old recording. A solo violin carries a yearning theme over sustained low strings, swelling toward a big romantic climax.

gouache-landscape.name: Opaque gouache landscape
gouache-landscape.still: Opaque gouache painting, the paint covering the whole surface with no gaps. Light greens and pale gold fill about 60% of the frame, green the largest share of that; coal-black darks and slate blues make up the rest, with small yellow accents and other colours mixed from these. Ragged directional strokes, two to five times as long as wide; broken dark dashes outline the edges of forms; dark masses flecked with lighter green and slate knife marks. Low late-afternoon side light, rims on the edges of forms, slight vignette and grain. Seen from slightly above in true perspective, a line leading the eye into depth, small repeated forms stepping into the distance. Avoid: watercolour transparency, vector fills, mud.
gouache-landscape.shot: A slow lateral track while the brushstrokes stir gently, as if in a breeze. The next view arrives as a fresh layer of opaque strokes brushed across the frame, covering the old one completely.
gouache-landscape.sound: A wordless male-voice choir humming in close, warm harmony over a gently rolling harp and low strings, like a 1940s valley hymn. Moderate walking tempo, tender and nostalgic, with a soft pipe-organ swell under the final bars.

loose-watercolour.name: Offset-line loose watercolour
loose-watercolour.still: Loose watercolour with quick ink line, colour first and line second, never aligned. Transparent washes cover most of the frame: cobalt for cool areas and shade (about a third), lemon for lit areas (about a third), rose for warm planes; bare paper 20 to 30%. Washes run oversized and slide one way off their objects, with wet edges, pooled rims and granulation; overlaps turn violet or green, never brown. Over them, thin blue-black ink draws the whole scene densely with flicked ends, straight edges overshooting corners, and wherever the scene has trees or clouds, they become looped strings. Lively, airy composition crowded with small details and bouncing figures. Avoid: muddy colour, lines tracing the colour, sparse line.
loose-watercolour.shot: Small, bouncy push-ins in time with the rhythm over the finished painting, the washes still wet and blooming softly at their edges. It ends with a brush-edge wipe or a page turning over to a fresh sheet.
loose-watercolour.sound: A bright, bouncing 1950s orchestral dance number with clarinet, muted trumpet and pizzicato strings at a brisk tempo with a light swing. Glockenspiel sparkles ride on top, airy and joyful like a sunny city morning.

social-realist-tempera.name: Blotted-line tempera realism
social-realist-tempera.still: 1950s social-realist tempera on warm board. Restrained colour by role: slate for cool areas and shade, about a third; brick and ochre for warm areas and clothes, about half; warm off-white board and ink for the rest; other colours are these darkened or greyed, plus one warm accent on the focal form. Ink lines jitter and wander, each outline broken into two or three unclosed strokes, sometimes doubled by a faint blotted ghost. Flat colour blocks sit slightly off the line, rough-edged and streaked with dry brush; modelled only with a darker flat of the same hue. Heavy, plain, frontal composition; big heads and hands on any people. Avoid: smooth gradients, clean closed outlines, cheerful colour.
social-realist-tempera.shot: Short, deliberate push-ins and a slow tilt up, settling on a close framing. The next image is pulled like a fresh print: the trembling ink line blots in first, then the flat colour blocks drop in slightly off register.
social-realist-tempera.sound: A sparse 1950s small-ensemble piece: a lone muted trumpet and low clarinet over a slow walking double bass and brushed snare. Tense, weary and urban, with one low brass note swelling like a distant ship's horn.

epic-poster-gouache.name: Painted epic film poster
epic-poster-gouache.still: Hand-painted 1960s epic film-poster art: gouache with oil highlights. A hard warm-cool split: cobalt across about the upper half of the frame, fading to pale blue and warming to cream near a low main light; amber over most of the rest; ochre-red for earthy surfaces, skin and costume; violet in distant shadows. A solid opaque mid-tone base, then directional strokes following each form, three values per form, soft-blended edges, dry brush only on dust and cloth, sharp warm-cream highlights last on lit edges. Light board grain, warm vignette, haze. The focal form centred and largest in a strong diagonal gesture, smaller looser shapes receding behind. Avoid: scratchy uniform hatching, flat digital fills, cold-only colour.
epic-poster-gouache.shot: A gently bouncing slow push from the wide to a low-angle close framing against the cobalt backdrop. It exits on a fast whip pan that smears the gouache into streaks of colour.
epic-poster-gouache.sound: A grand 1960s symphonic theme: sweeping strings in broad unison, booming timpani and a soaring French horn, with a hand drum and a modal woodwind melody. Slow and majestic, building to a huge heroic swell.

tudor-court-portrait.name: Renaissance court portrait in oil
tudor-court-portrait.still: Sixteenth-century court portrait in oil, built in layers: a toned underlayer, form-following strokes, soft glazes and fine detail last, with a smooth finish. A deep green curtain fills about half the frame, black and velvet red most of the rest, with gold and fur brown in the details and warm, fully modelled flesh tones. Each material has its own handling: fur hair by hair, velvet folds with sharp light ridges, metal with two highlights per piece. Formal half-length pose before the curtain, the wider setting seen through a window or told by an object held; soft light from upper left; warm varnish and fine craquelure. Avoid: flat fills, hard digital edges, even light.
tudor-court-portrait.shot: A slow push from the whole formal portrait in to a close study of fur, velvet and metal, the soft light from the upper left flickering warmly across them like candlelight. It ends as that light gutters and the varnished picture sinks into darkness.
tudor-court-portrait.sound: Renaissance consort music: a lute picking a slow pavane over soft viols and a quiet recorder, at a stately walking pace. Grave, intimate and candlelit, with the dry warmth of a wood-panelled room.

chiaroscuro-oil.name: Top-light chiaroscuro oil
chiaroscuro-oil.still: Chiaroscuro oil painting under a single overhead light. About 70% of the frame is readable warm dark, mostly umber, with near-black only in the deepest corners; amber mid-tones take about 20%; upward-facing planes reach a warm pale gold; one deep red accent. Darks are thin smooth glazes, lights thick ridged impasto, the modelling soft, never scratchy; amber varnish, heavy vignette, fine linen grain. The focal form stands in the pool of light, which covers at least a quarter of the frame height, its upper planes casting shadow downward; a warm opening such as a window may glow behind. Avoid: lifted darks, flat light, forms popping out, frames too dark to read.
chiaroscuro-oil.shot: Slow, patient push-ins and pull-backs in the dark, the overhead light staying fixed as the only key. The shot closes as darkness glazes over the pool of light, a deep amber fade to black.
chiaroscuro-oil.sound: A slow, melancholy waltz on solo mandolin and soft accordion, answered by a lone trumpet over hushed low strings. Warm, old-world and grave, in a gentle three-beat time with plenty of space.

american-scene-realism.name: Slanting-sunlight realist oil
american-scene-realism.still: Quiet mid-century realist oil painting in large flat planes of restrained, pale colour. Light and mid sage greens and cream fill most of the frame, with grey-green for the lower planes, about a quarter; a few hard-edged parallelograms of warm sunlight fall across the planes, crossed by crisp straight shadows where the scene has window frames or railings. Each plane carries a few long dragged strokes over a fine linen texture. Figures are built from three or four overlapping soft-edged value shapes, no outline, real proportions, standing apart. Signature view: the scene seen still and straight on in one-point perspective, low side light laid across the lower planes. Avoid: heavy outlines, vector shapes, dark saturated planes, fuzzy light patches.
american-scene-realism.shot: The camera stays locked for most of the five seconds; whatever moves does so slowly and quietly, and the sunlight also creeps across the planes. Then one sudden event in under a second, such as a whip pan or a burst of light; a burst blows the frame to a warm flat white that settles into the next plane of colour.
american-scene-realism.sound: A spare 1970s chamber piece: an eerie glass-like tone over a slow, hesitant piano and a quiet low drum pulse. Lonely, still and slightly uneasy, opening into a brief burst of warmth at the end.

egg-tempera.name: Egg tempera on gesso
egg-tempera.still: Egg tempera on a gesso panel: dry, matte and very fine, colour built from dense hairline cross-hatched strokes. Muted palette: pale overcast grey across about 40% of the frame, straw yellow about a third, umber, misty grey-green and rust in the rest; everything else mixed from these, with at most one small accent of brighter colour. Where the scene has ground, lay it as big light and dark patches, then fine strokes, dark tufts and single wind-combed blades; where there are rocks or buildings, hatch them along their planes; light sources as small pale dots without halo. Empty, lonely space around the focal form, which sits off-centre under soft overcast light. Avoid: wet watercolour blooms, saturated colour, thick shiny strokes.
egg-tempera.shot: A slow sideways drift or a quiet push-in; along with what moves above, where the picture has grass blades, they also stir in the wind. A circular black iris closes in on the focal point to end the shot.
egg-tempera.sound: A sparse, contemplative piece for solo classical guitar, picked slowly with long gaps, over a soft sustained string drone. Cold, pale and lonely, like wind over an empty upland in late autumn.

transparent-watercolour.name: Autumn transparent watercolour
transparent-watercolour.still: Transparent watercolour glazed in layers on cold-press paper. Cool grey-blue mist and pale washes fill about half the frame, violet-grey shadows about a fifth; autumn gold, scarlet and rust take the accents and any foliage, and any ground is pale green-ochre. Crisp shapes first, then two or three smaller, darker glazes drying to tide-mark edges; a few blooms inside large washes; light granulation; broad soft areas wet-in-wet, and any sky or water too; fine textures in dry brush, and any ripples too. White paper is the brightest white and stays bare for highlights. Light from one side; any leaves as scallop-edged clusters with dark dots, and loose leaves flicked out with the brush. Avoid: opaque gouache, airbrushed blur, vector edges, muddy colour, saturated sunsets.
transparent-watercolour.shot: A long, slow lateral move across one continuous painted sheet; where the picture has leaves, some drift past the lens. It closes with a mist wash that fades the picture back to blank paper, or a page turning to a new sheet; no hard cuts.
transparent-watercolour.sound: Gentle acoustic music: felt piano and fingerpicked guitar with a soft woodwind line and light strings, slow and unhurried. Quiet, autumnal and a little sad, with a faint breeze over water underneath.

gongbi-silk.name: Gongbi colour on silk
gongbi-silk.still: Chinese gongbi court painting in heavy mineral colour on aged silk. Empty areas and the background stay a mid-value warm silk ochre over about half the frame; cinnabar, azurite, malachite, gamboge and gold fill the forms, all calmed by a final warm ochre glaze. Each form gets a flat base, a wash darkening its lower and overlapped edges, an even iron-wire outline in dark brown, then gold and white lifts; no cast shadows or glare; where the scene has water, it runs in fine-line ripples; where it has buildings, they are ruled, every tile drawn; where it has a crowd, no two figures repeat. Faint silk weave, brown vignette. Symmetrical one-point composition, a large figure or form before a deep, ordered space. Avoid: copy-pasted figures, unwashed flat fills, loose ink wash, poster saturation.
gongbi-silk.shot: A slow, stately push toward the centre of the symmetrical scene, the camera never tilting. The shot ends as a silk curtain or a hand scroll unrolls across the frame to reveal the next painted view.
gongbi-silk.sound: Chinese court ceremonial music: deep bronze bells and stone chimes struck slowly over a sustained reed mouth organ and a bamboo flute. Solemn, spacious and grand, at a slow processional tempo with a soft drum pulse.

frontier-western-oil.name: Frontier sunset and nocturne oil
frontier-western-oil.still: Western frontier oil painting with loaded strokes, in one of two keys, chosen by the scene's time of day. Before dark: red-gold light, orange into deep red, laid in long horizontal strokes; where the scene shows sky it takes 50 to 60% of the frame with the sun low on the horizon, and where it shows none the same red-gold light falls in through the openings; the subject and other figures dark and warm against the light with a thin warm rim on the side facing it, the subject's face and clothes still clearly readable in warm reflected light. After dark: a blue-green nocturne: deep teal for the darks and any sky, pale green moonlit edges, warm yellow window light falling on dark surfaces where the scene has windows, with rain wherever the scene is open to the sky. Broad readable shapes first, then strokes three to six times as long as wide with soft broken ends, close in value to the colour beneath, following each surface; light linen texture. Where a horizon shows it sits low; the subject medium in frame, other figures small. Avoid: smooth gradients, hard-edged flat bands, shattered shapes, grey figures in warm scenes.
frontier-western-oil.shot: One slow push in from the opening frame toward the subject, with no wide pans. Along with what moves, from a before-dark still the red-gold light sinks and fades until the frame cools into the blue-green night palette; from an after-dark still, where the picture has rain it keeps falling, and where it has lit windows their light flickers.
frontier-western-oil.sound: A slow, sparse frontier ballad on solo acoustic guitar, picked gently, with a lonely harmonica and a low bowed bass. Weathered, elegiac and quiet, at an unhurried tempo full of open space.

blue-oil-portrait.name: Moonlit blue oil portrait
blue-oil-portrait.still: Night oil portraiture: smooth volumes repainted in two passes of short, low-contrast strokes that follow the form, broad on the background and cloth, fine and smooth on skin. Mid blue-violet covers about 60% of the frame across the background and its far planes; moonlit planes turn pale lavender-blue; teal lights any water or gloss and the lit sides; magenta appears only as a soft rim; the deepest shadows a near-black navy. Skin takes blue top planes and a wet highlight. One key light, cool full moonlight that breaks into a glitter path on any water or gloss; other lights small cyan-white points; fine grain. Signature framing: the focal form calm, about two thirds of frame height. Avoid: coarse dabs, a lifeless statue look, a murky frame.
blue-oil-portrait.shot: A slow, steady push-in that holds the calm mood while the moonlit glints shimmer wherever the picture has them. It ends as a wave of deep blue strokes washes across the frame and repaints it into the next image.
blue-oil-portrait.sound: Slow chamber strings with a solo cello and soft piano chords, drifting in a minor key with long reverberant tails and a faint, slowed-down warm bass. Tender, intimate and dreamlike, like a calm sea at night.

soft-pastel.name: Dusk soft pastel
soft-pastel.still: Soft pastel on grey-violet toned paper, the paper tooth showing everywhere as fine speckle. The upper part of the frame, about half, is a smooth field of dusk light (the sky itself where the scene shows sky): gold low, rose above, violet highest and in a few long thin bands; dusk blue for shadows. The lower half carries the texture: dry-grass ochre for the ground and lower surfaces under fine upright strokes, dense in front and thinning toward the back; objects get soft diagonal hatching and broken edges. A long horizontal line near mid-frame separates the smooth light from the textured lower half; the focal form mid-sized in the lower half; any lamps glow warm against the dusk light. Avoid: oily impasto, sharp edges, bare smooth ground.
soft-pastel.shot: One slow pan with a light push-in while the dusk light drifts from gold to rose to violet and any warm lamps brighten. At the end the light fades into the grey-violet of the paper itself, as if the colour were rubbed back off.
soft-pastel.sound: A minimal, meditative piano piece of slow, sparse notes with long sustain, joined by a soft string pad and a distant open-air breeze. Gentle, wistful and quiet, at a very slow tempo like dusk over an empty plain.

portrait-miniature.name: Locket portrait miniature
portrait-miniature.still: Sixteenth-century portrait miniature in opaque watercolour on warm vellum. The oval takes about half the frame, an ultramarine ground showing in its open spaces; shell gold in granular flecks with a few burnished highlights; carmine, lead white and verdigris in the details. Colour laid flat, very fine hatching in shadows, lead-white dots on lit edges, red-brown outlines; where the scene shows land or sky, it is laid in flat colour bands. Signature framing: the picture inside a gold-rimmed oval locket lying on rust-red damask, a flowering white wild-rose briar twining along the inside of the oval's rim around the focal point, a short motto in the language of this prompt, in gold Roman capitals, arcing along the top. Avoid: airbrush gradients, thick oil strokes, flat yellow gold.
portrait-miniature.shot: A slow push in with a slight tilt down over the locket, the wild-rose flowers and the damask stirring gently. The shot ends as the locket's gold lid swings shut across the frame.
portrait-miniature.sound: Sixteenth-century chamber music: a lute and a soft virginal playing a graceful galliard under a quiet recorder melody. Courtly, delicate and romantic, at a light, lilting tempo.

illuminated-manuscript.name: Gilded manuscript page
illuminated-manuscript.still: An illuminated manuscript page, cropped or an open spread, filling the frame. Vellum covers about half; burnished gold leaf on raised gesso with punched dot rosettes fills at least a tenth; lapis and vermilion carry the colour, with brown ink outlines. Gothic figures in flat colour and ink line; interlace knotwork, ivy borders and marginal grotesques; broad-nib script with gothic, textura-like strokes, written in the language of this prompt, with red-and-blue line fillers and one large gilded first character. The main picture is a window about half the page beside a text column, on gold leaf or night-blue grounds strewn with gold stars; figures may break the frame. Warm candlelight from upper left, brown vignette, faint pigment grain. Avoid: flat yellow for gold, modern typefaces, glints on figures.
illuminated-manuscript.shot: A slow push into the page with layered parallax while a candle glint sweeps across the gold leaf only. Toward the end the candlelight flickers softly over the vellum and the gilded first character gleams.
illuminated-manuscript.sound: Medieval music: a slow, wordless drone of low male voices with a hurdy-gurdy, frame drum and wooden pipe. Austere and ancient at first, then a steady martial drum and a bagpipe drone build toward a stirring call to arms.

gothic-charcoal.name: Gothic charcoal drawing
gothic-charcoal.still: Vine and compressed charcoal on fine-toothed paper. Outside the subject, the values run dark: about 60% of the frame in dark-to-mid greys, 15% velvet black in the nearest foreground and largest masses, small clean-paper lights; near-black charcoal on warm off-white paper. Broken vine lines, side-of-stick sweeps following the form, hatching and finger smudges, with grain only in the midtones; edges, glows and horizontal mist are lifted out with an eraser. Only the subject keeps its own colours, laid in fairly solid pastel with the tooth peeking through and a charcoal outline, while the rest stays in the style's charcoal black and paper white. Moonlight from above, two or three mist bands, dark looming foreground forms. Avoid: digital noise, smooth digital glows, grey blacks, empty bright skies.
gothic-charcoal.shot: A slow subjective push forward while the nearest dark forms part to either side and mist bands drift across at different speeds. The shot closes with an eraser lifting a band of light out of the charcoal, or a finger-smudged dark sweep wiping the paper back to tone.
gothic-charcoal.sound: Brooding late-1930s Gothic suspense: slow chamber strings with trembling tremolo, a low harp figure, a lonely solo oboe and a faint wordless choir pad, about 60 BPM. Misty hall reverb and swelling dynamics that never fully resolve, dark and romantic.

graphite-magazine.name: 1940s magazine pencil illustration
graphite-magazine.still: Graphite pencil in the finished, controlled manner of a 1940s magazine illustration, on lightly toothed warm white paper with dark grey lead. The frame is toned almost edge to edge: the setting fully drawn in mid-greys, about 15% dark accents, only about the outer tenth fading into loose margins. Faint construction lines show beneath pressure-tapered contours that overshoot at corners; one to four near-parallel hatching passes follow the form, then rubbed tone and eraser lifts. Only the subject keeps its own colours, in coloured pencil over the graphite, while the rest stays in the style's graphite greys and paper white. Close, dramatic framing with one strong focal point. Avoid: cross-hatched grids, scribbly sketching, a near-empty page.
graphite-magazine.shot: Along with what moves, the drawing keeps its finished pencil look while the camera eases slowly back, a few hatching strokes deepening in the shadows. A transition is a cut to a closer view, or the eraser lifting the old image back to bare paper as a new one is drawn.
graphite-magazine.sound: 1940s small-orchestra mood music: muted trumpet, warm clarinet, brushed snare, walking upright bass and soft strings, around 100 BPM. Polished and polite on the surface with a wry, slightly uneasy undertone, in a dry room.

one-line-caricature.name: Single-line ink caricature
one-line-caricature.still: Pen-and-ink caricature on white paper in near-black ink. Outside the subject, about 60% stays paper white, roughly 25% is thin line work and 15% solid black in dark clothing, hair and large objects; grey only as sparse parallel hatching. Lines are elastic, long and continuous, one stroke per contour, fine at the ends and swelling on curves. Only the subject keeps its own colours, every one of them filled flat as its own area inside the line, while the rest stays in the style's black ink and white paper. The setting is fully drawn in thin line with white space between objects, and the subject's most characteristic feature is gleefully exaggerated. Avoid: stiff limbs, stick figures, a bare setting.
one-line-caricature.shot: Starting from the finished drawing, the camera travels along its long, continuous contour lines, then eases back to the whole composed drawing and ends with a slight push-in. No cuts; whatever moves stays drawn in the same elastic, continuous ink line.
one-line-caricature.sound: One solo instrument playing one unbroken melodic line, such as a cello, clarinet or harp, light and witty at around 90 BPM, with quick short notes for fast passages and, where it pauses, a single long note fading into near silence. A rare plucked accent is the only second colour; dry, intimate room, no pads.

ink-wash-cartoon.name: Ink-and-wash gag cartoon
ink-wash-cartoon.still: A single-panel magazine cartoon in nib-pen ink and light watercolour, full bleed with no border, on cold-press paper fading to white at the edges. Pale washes with pooled edges cover most objects, slipping just past the lines: grey and slate blue lead, sand fills the middle, a little rust as the accent, and about a third stays bare paper. Nib lines are thin on straights, swell in turns and flick off at the ends; box corners overlap. Exaggerated, expressive drawing among everyday props, with one short hand-lettered deadpan caption beneath in the language of this prompt. Avoid: saturated colour, uniform vector lines, a small framed panel floating in white.
ink-wash-cartoon.shot: Whatever moves stays drawn in nib ink and wash, and living things add a slight hand-drawn wobble; the camera drifts and pushes in gently over the drawing and its caption. A transition is the panel splitting into two drawings side by side, or a fresh wash flooding across the paper.
ink-wash-cartoon.sound: 1970s city-comedy jazz: a light piano trio with brushed drums and walking upright bass, a wistful clarinet carrying the melody, about 110 BPM. Dry, intimate and gently neurotic, with playful pauses.

crayon-drawing.name: Child's wax-crayon drawing
crayon-drawing.still: A careful six-to-eight-year-old's wax-crayon drawing on white paper. Primary box colours, red, orange, yellow, green and blue, fill most shapes, with 40–60% paper showing where pressure is light and overlaps showing through. Waxy, wobbling black or dark-brown outlines; back-and-forth scribble fills that overshoot the edges, each area in its own direction and unevenly dense, catching only the peaks of the paper grain. Child conventions: a ground line, flattened perspective, arrowed labels in wobbly crayon in the language of this prompt, a smiling sun when the sky is in view, one mirrored letter. Avoid: neat adult rendering, random scrawl, regular mesh or stipple, smooth gradients.
crayon-drawing.shot: The camera moves over a large page: a slightly shaky push toward the main figure, then a calm drift across the drawing while the crayon lines gently boil. A transition is colouring over the page or a page turn; never a dissolve.
crayon-drawing.sound: A small toy-box ensemble: ukulele, clarinet, music box, glockenspiel and toy piano, with a recorder singing a simple lilting tune over light shaker and woodblock, around 100 BPM. Warm, playful and innocent, with a full beat of silence after a little stumble.

pen-wash-sketch.name: Reportage pen-and-wash sketch
pen-wash-sketch.still: A reportage field sketch in pen and transparent wash on sketchbook paper. Bold washes with soft wet edges, blooms and uneven pigment cover about 70% of the frame, shifted slightly off the line: olive, ochre and smoke grey carry most of it, skin in diluted ochre, one hot accent for light sources and for any sky the scene shows. Fast, confident warm-black pen lines with flicked ends and overshooting corners; quick hatching and zigzags for shadow; light paper grain. Bare paper only in highlights, a thin band along the four edges and brush gaps, with a one-line scrawled pencil note of place, time and weather in a corner, in the language of this prompt. Avoid: a polished finish, an empty page, muddy washes, heavy noise.
pen-wash-sketch.shot: A lagging handheld follow or a lateral track across the page, then a push-in on the moment that matters, a few quick new pen lines appearing on their own and a drop of wash spreading after them. A transition is a page turn to a new spread or colour spreading from a wet front; no dissolves.
pen-wash-sketch.sound: Open-air sketching music: solo nylon-string guitar with a light café accordion and brushed percussion, a gentle waltz in three at about 95 BPM. Airy and observant, with a bar of near silence before the next phrase.

travel-journal.name: Field-journal pencil and watercolour
travel-journal.still: A 19th-century field journal come to life: full-colour transparent watercolour over visible pencil on yellowed rag paper with faint stains and foxing. Rich warm washes cover about 80% of the frame: dusty-rose washes in the upper frame turning lavender at the top, ochre-gold washes below, violet in the farthest planes, long shadows and pale-gold lifts on sun-facing edges. The pressure-varied, broken pencil under-drawing reads through soft wet edges, blooms, pooled rims and granulation. Small iron-gall ink labels, arrows and margin notes, handwritten in the language of this prompt; a taped sketch, a hand-drawn map or a pressed flower may crowd the page edges. Low magic-hour sun. Avoid: grey or muddy washes, uniform digital outlines, flat polygons.
travel-journal.shot: One slow push-in over the finished page, the washes still glistening and one last wash spreading in the foreground, carries on until the page edges slide out of frame. After that, a gentle lateral follow; a transition is a page turn to a new spread or colour arriving from a wet front, never a dissolve.
travel-journal.sound: Gentle travel-journal music: solo nylon-string guitar and a warm clarinet over soft pizzicato strings, an unhurried waltz in three at about 80 BPM. Wide, wistful and sunlit, leaving breathing room between phrases.

technical-line-art.name: Technical-manual line art
technical-line-art.still: A military technical-manual illustration in uniform black ink on warm off-white paper with a faint engineering grid. Flat olive and sand tints cover only 20–30% of the drawing; the rest is line and paper. Even outlines, thinner hatching for all shading, stippled ground, and light drawn as ray lines rather than glows. A one-point-perspective main view fills most of the page; around it sit exploded views of the key object along a dash-dot axis, circled numbers on leader lines, a parts table, warning and caution boxes, typewriter labels, figure numbers (all lettering in the language of this prompt) and a black chapter card. Avoid: gradient shading, too much colour, decorative fonts, sparse pages.
technical-line-art.shot: Animated on twos, whatever moves going in small held steps, and the exploded parts also slide apart along their dash-dot axes. The camera opens on the whole page with a slow push, then cuts to an enlarged inset as if turning to the next figure; a transition is a figure number rewritten or a new page sliding in.
technical-line-art.sound: Tense procedural minimalism: a low sustained drone, dry clock-like ticking percussion, sparse metallic hits and a muted pulsing bass, about 70 BPM. Close, controlled and dry, the tension rising slowly without release.

section-axonometric.name: Architectural section axonometric
section-axonometric.still: A vector architectural section axonometric in a low dimetric view: the cut face lies along a near-flat 7° axis facing us, depth runs along a 42° axis at half scale, roof and near walls cut away to show what is inside. The section cuts through the scene's building or ground. Default daylight, with a pale sky where the scene shows sky. Concrete grey and earth brown take about half the drawing; the rest is oak, charcoal, pine green and white, with green for lawn and translucent blue for water wherever the scene has them. Poché on cut faces, dark concrete with aggregate and earth hatched at 45° with stones; thin 1 px dark-grey lines throughout; furnished rooms where the cut opens them, and simple scale figures. The whole drawing fills about 80% of the frame. Avoid: 30° isometric, thick outlines, a small drawing.
section-axonometric.shot: The camera cranes slowly along the section in one continuous path, framing two or three spaces of the cut at a time and, where the cut shows more than one level, passing through the slabs between levels, then settles on the whole drawing. A transition is the section line sweeping across to reveal a new cut; no cuts within the path.
section-axonometric.sound: Stately baroque-flavoured chamber music: harpsichord, string quartet and light piano, measured and elegant at about 90 BPM, with a low cello undertone that slowly grows darker beneath the poise.

cyanotype-blueprint.name: Cyanotype engineering blueprint
cyanotype-blueprint.still: A cyanotype engineering blueprint filling the frame: mottled Prussian-blue paper covers about 85% of it, with uneven exposure, a greenish over-exposed margin, creases and faint water stains. White lines are sharp but printed: outlines heavier than hatching and dimensions, broken where exposure was weak, with a slight cyan bloom. Everything is drawn densely in drafting grammar: elevations, sections, detail circles, dimension chains, hidden lines, single-stroke lettering and a title block, all lettering in the language of this prompt. Red-pencil notes, arrows and revision clouds are the only warm marks on the sheet. A walnut drafting table appears only at the very edges. Avoid: neon glow, clean digital blue, sparse sheets.
cyanotype-blueprint.shot: Starting on the finished drawing, the camera makes a slow layered-parallax push-in, then cuts on a downbeat to a two-times detail view. A transition is the drawing number in the title block struck through in red pencil and rewritten, or a section line sweeping across; no dissolves.
cyanotype-blueprint.sound: Contrapuntal mechanical chamber music: harpsichord, bassoon, spiccato strings, harp and celesta in interlocking imitative lines, a short repeated motive turning like a gear, about 108 BPM. Precise, dry and quietly wondrous, landing on a clean final cadence.

typewriter-art.name: Typewriter character art
typewriter-art.still: The picture is typed: one bold monospaced glyph per key on a fixed grid; cells about 1/150 of frame width and twice as tall, on cream paper. 85–95% of cells are struck, bare paper only in highlights, darks about 30% as overstrikes like M#. Tone comes from a key ladder (light . : -, mid = + o, dark X # M); each material repeats its own keys, uneven ribbon ink, a few keys always high or low. Only the subject keeps its own colours, struck in coloured ribbon, while the rest stays in the style's black ink on cream paper. Hard sidelight casts long crisp shadows, and shapes read as clear silhouettes and crisp-edged blocks of glyphs. Avoid: sparse frames, shapeless horizontal streaks.
typewriter-art.shot: From the finished typed picture, whatever moves is retyped glyph by glyph while the camera pushes in as the cells grow until a few glyphs fill the frame, or the paper scrolls up line by line. A transition is a hard redraw: the sheet advances and the next image types itself over fresh paper.
typewriter-art.sound: An original analog-synth bed, never chiptune: one slow arpeggio from a sawtooth oscillator through a resonant filter that gradually opens, a soft sub-bass drone, long reverb on pads and a slight tape wobble, about 84 BPM. Sparse and nocturnal, with crisp mechanical key clicks as rhythmic accents and near silence between phrases.

scrimshaw.name: Engraved whale-tooth scrimshaw
scrimshaw.still: Scrimshaw: a 19th-century sailor's needle engraving on a broad, flat polished whale tooth lying horizontal on an oak table, filling about 85% of the frame width. Warm ivory with growth bands, scratches and a honey tip; near-black engraving covers about 70% of the tooth's surface, with red, blue and yellow only as small touches. Fine needle hatching, swelling outlines and stipple, dense in the main figure and foreground, light in open background areas; any sea drawn as rows of stylised waves. The central figure is large, about a third of the tooth's height, and lightly hand-coloured. Folk layout: rope border, a ribbon motto in the language of this prompt, rayed sun; shaded edges and one gloss streak. Avoid: thick lines, solid fills, a slim horn.
scrimshaw.shot: Start on the whole tooth on the table and push in until it fills the frame, then pan slowly left to right across the engraving as the engraved scene begins to move. A transition is a glint of light sweeping across the polished ivory, or the needle scratching a new line that becomes the next image.
scrimshaw.sound: Instrumental 19th-century seafaring folk: fiddle, concertina, acoustic guitar and a soft frame drum in a lilting 6/8 at about 100 BPM. Warm, salty and heartfelt, with a gentle swell like rolling water.

art-deco-poster.name: Black-and-gold Art Deco poster
art-deco-poster.still: A 1920s Art Deco revue poster printed on a black lacquer ground. Colour: black fills about half the frame; gold with pale highlights and silver take most of the rest, each metal built from three to five hard-edged gradient bands; skin is a pale silver-cream. Airbrushed glows, sunburst rays, ziggurat steps and streamlined curves, with fine grain, glints and small stars. Frontal symmetry on a centre axis, a stepped gold proscenium of lines and bulbs around the scene, one central spotlight; figures elongated with real faces. Avoid: flat yellow for metal, faceless figures, extra hues.
art-deco-poster.shot: The camera pushes slowly along the centre axis while marquee bulbs chase and a gold sheen sweeps across the metal on the beat, with rings of light radiating from the main source. The shot closes as two Deco door leaves swing shut along the centre seam, never a plain dissolve.
art-deco-poster.sound: A late-1920s symphonic jazz foxtrot at a bright medium tempo: stride piano, muted trumpet, clarinet trills and glissandi, a sax section, pizzicato walking bass and brushed snare. Harp glissandi and a xylophone run add glitter; the mood is glamorous, buoyant and theatrical.

expressionist-woodcut.name: Expressionist woodcut
expressionist-woodcut.still: An expressionist woodcut printed from carved blocks. Outside the subject, solid black ink covers sixty to seventy percent of the frame on cream paper, with no grey midtones. White knife cuts, each tapering in and out with chipped edges, separate the forms; cuts widen near the light and run in slightly uneven bundles, over wood-grain streaks and under-inked speckle. Only the subject keeps its own colours, each laid as a flat colour area with the cuts printed over them, while everything else stays black ink on cream paper. Forms fill the frame and are cropped by its edges; light comes from a single direction, and the deepest shadows around the subject stay uncut black. Avoid: grey fog, even striped hatching, gore.
expressionist-woodcut.shot: Camera moves are few: the framing stays almost steady, with at most one slow push or pan, and whatever moves does so slowly and quietly. The transition is the print itself: a hard cut to a fresh impression, or the wet sheet peeled off the block to reveal the next image; never a dissolve.
expressionist-woodcut.sound: Sparse, slow and grave, around 60 beats per minute: low strings in pizzicato and spiccato, a frame drum and woodblock, timpani rolls and a single tam-tam stroke. A bowed saw or hurdy-gurdy drone sits under long silences; the mood is solemn and mournful.

letterpress-engraving.name: Newsprint letterpress engraving
letterpress-engraving.still: An 1890s newspaper front page printed by letterpress, with one large line engraving. Warm black ink on yellowed newsprint. Outside the subject, ink covers about a third of the page, paper the rest. Type shows ink spread, ragged edges, under-inked patches and mirrored show-through; the picture is all hatching that follows the form, cross-hatched only in the darks, with heavier shadow-side contours. Only the subject keeps its own colours, each colour printed from a separate plate slightly off register, while the rest stays warm black on newsprint. Layout: a masthead, a grained wood-type headline across the full width in the language of this prompt, three to six columns of small type flanking the picture. Avoid: clean digital type, smooth grey shading, other colours outside the subject.
letterpress-engraving.shot: The camera moves like a loupe over the sheet: a push in on the printed sheet as the press thumps on each beat, then a slow pan along the columns at reading distance. The transition is a new sheet pulled off the press or a page turning; no dissolves or wipes.
letterpress-engraving.sound: A dry, ticking chamber piece at a brisk walking tempo: plucked harpsichord and pizzicato string quartet, with a solo cello line that sustains only at the turns. The rhythm runs steady and mechanical like a printing press; the mood is urgent and earnest.

public-works-silkscreen.name: 1930s public-works silkscreen
public-works-silkscreen.still: A 1930s public-works silkscreen poster in six opaque inks printed light to dark on rag paper. Cream covers the lights (about a quarter), ochre and vermilion the backdrop and warm planes (about two fifths), teal the cool planes and shade, and a brown keyline last. Shadows are a darker ink overprinted, never grey; big areas use coarse split-fountain blends. Screens sit one to three pixels off register, with wandering stencil edges, squeegee streaks and warm paper grain on every flat. Simplified planes, crescent shadows, the main form filling half to two thirds of the frame height, and a bold capital title band in the language of this prompt. Avoid: halftone dots, smooth gradients, clean vector flats.
public-works-silkscreen.shot: The camera trucks slowly across the finished print while its ink colours pulse on the beat, then pushes gently toward the centre. The transition is the squeegee itself: a diagonal sweep that prints the next poster behind the blade; no dissolves.
public-works-silkscreen.sound: Warm acoustic folk of the 1930s at an easygoing medium tempo: strummed guitar, harmonica, fiddle, banjo and upright bass with light brushes. Each new layer brings in one instrument; the mood is hopeful, homespun and communal.

wartime-lithograph.name: Wartime stone lithograph
wartime-lithograph.still: A 1940s wartime stone-lithograph poster on foxed cream paper. Cream for paper and highlights about two fifths, grey-blue for cool areas and shadow about a third, brick red, deep green and navy as accents under a quarter. Three plates sit one to three pixels off register: flat colour fills, a grey-blue crayon shadow plate with short slanted stone grain or coarse 45-degree halftone bands, and a green-black keyline around every shape. Wherever the scene shows sky it is airbrushed; pale angled light bands cancel the shadow plate. Frontal, symmetrical staging with the main form set before a huge graphic shape such as a flag or a plain banner. Avoid: clean vector edges, perfect registration, big saturated fields. Avoid radiating sun rays or sunburst backgrounds.
wartime-lithograph.shot: Slow drifts with slight parallax between the printed layers, a tilt up toward the sky where the picture has one, and one crisp pull-back that leaves the main form small before the big graphic shape. Along with what moves, the paper grain boils at twelve frames a second; the shot changes as a newly printed sheet is laid over the old one.
wartime-lithograph.sound: A 1940s home-front orchestral march at a steady moderate tempo: snare drum, brass fanfare, warm strings and a rising horn line. A hymn-like brass chorale swells in the middle; the mood is resolute, stoic and hopeful.

wood-type-poster.name: Wood-type rally poster
wood-type-poster.still: A letterpress poster printed from wood type and carved cuts on cream stock. Three inks: blue for cool areas and shadow masses (about a third), red for warm surfaces and stripes (about a quarter), black for outlines and type. Each ink sits two to four pixels off register; solids show wood grain, pinholed starved patches and squeezed edges; mid-tones are coarse halftone dots on no more than a third of the frame. Forms are cut like linocuts, with heavy outlines, gouged white lines and crescent shadows. Imagery fills about seventy percent of the frame, with one or two short wood-type lines in the language of this prompt on banners and signs, with offset shadows. Avoid: busy grey mid-tones, perfect registration.
wood-type-poster.shot: Small pushes and a lateral track, with a quick bump of the camera on each strong beat (every two seconds without music). The transition is a fresh sheet slammed onto the press bed and pulled away to reveal the next print.
wood-type-poster.sound: Brassy small-town rally music of the late 1940s at a quick march tempo: a brass band with snare, bass drum, cymbals and tuba, plus a honky-tonk piano. Stomping on-beat accents; the mood is rousing, populist and loud.

circus-chromolithograph.name: Circus chromolithograph
circus-chromolithograph.still: A late-nineteenth-century circus chromolithograph printed from four stones on warm cream paper. Chrome yellow, vermilion and cobalt each take a fifth to a quarter of the frame, key black the outlines; overprints give only orange, green, brown, tan, pale blue and grey. Solids print flat; screened dots appear only on gradients such as skin, and on sky or ground where the scene shows them, each stone at its own angle and one to three pixels off register, over stone grain. Heavy black outlines, crescent shadows, light from the upper left. Exaggerated perspective with radial lines converging on the main action, several things happening at once; any crowd is many tiny distinct figures. Avoid: off-palette colours, dot-only crowds, pinkish screened flats.
circus-chromolithograph.shot: A tilt up across the scene to the action, then a lateral dolly along the scene, cutting at the peak of a movement. The transition is a stone-printed sheet peeling away to reveal the next poster.
circus-chromolithograph.sound: A racing circus galop: a brass band with cornet, trombone slides, oom-pah tuba, snare rolls and cymbals, plus a steam-organ calliope. Bright, boisterous and showy, with a drum roll building to a cymbal crash.

belle-epoque-lithograph.name: Belle Époque cabaret lithograph
belle-epoque-lithograph.still: A Belle Époque colour lithograph poster on cream stone-grained paper. Large flat plates with slightly wobbly edges: yellow and orange-red carry about half the frame; olive, a muted bottle green and a greyed mauve fill most of the rest; black for contours; flesh is orange-red thinned with paper. Outlines are drawn with a loaded brush: blunt start, swelling middle, split dry tail. Sparse toothbrush ink spatter falls only on shadow sides, cast shadows and glows, under fifteen percent of the frame, with grouped dry-brush streaks on large surfaces. Flat, even light; caricatured profiles; one large form in front, cropped by the frame edge. Avoid: halos, smooth gradients, regular halftone, all-over speckle.
belle-epoque-lithograph.shot: A slow lateral pan with shallow parallax between the flat colour layers, settling into a medium shot. Whatever moves stays in flat colour plates with wobbly brush outlines on the grained paper.
belle-epoque-lithograph.sound: A Parisian cabaret waltz at a lilting medium tempo: accordion, piano, violin and a light snare, with a clarinet answering the tune. Flirtatious, worldly and gently tipsy.

satirical-etching.name: Hand-coloured satirical engraving
satirical-etching.still: An eighteenth-century satirical print: a copperplate engraving coloured by hand. All line is brown-black: swelling burin outlines, heavier on the shadow side, and hatching that follows every form, cross-hatched in the darks and ruled on flat areas. Clear but strong watercolour washes cover nearly the whole picture and spill a few pixels past the lines: claret, brass, flesh and slate blue for about half, warm ochre and umber on large surfaces. Sepia laid paper, foxing, a plate mark. Busy comic staging: big-nosed caricature bystanders, props and animals around the centre, and one slanted handwritten speech balloon in the language of this prompt. Avoid: even mechanical hatching, blank paper, colour exactly inside the lines, muddy colour.
satirical-etching.shot: Hold the full plate for about two seconds, whip in to one detail, glide across the sheet to another, then settle on a close view. The transition is a tissue guard laid over the print or a fresh proof pulled from the copper; no dissolves.
satirical-etching.sound: A jaunty eighteenth-century country dance at a bouncing quick tempo: harpsichord, fiddle, recorder, bassoon and a light tabor. Comic pizzicato asides and sudden pauses; the mood is bawdy, cheeky and playful.

three-ink-stencil-print.name: Three-ink stencil print
three-ink-stencil-print.still: A three-ink stencil-duplicator print on warm white paper. Orange-red is the dominant field, about sixty percent, with vertical drip streaks; deep blue takes silhouettes and shadows, about a quarter; fluorescent pink only rims and halos. Each ink is halftoned at its own angle and misregistered two to four pixels, with grain, pinholes and slightly ragged edges. Orange is knocked out under blue so silhouettes print pure blue; only the darkest accents overprint two inks to near-black. Light is the absence of ink: beams, lamps and lit ground show bare paper ringed in pink. Night staging in strong silhouettes against the red field. The subject's face, shape and clothes stay readable, drawn in blue halftone detail rather than a flat silhouette. Avoid: blue-dominated frames, smooth gradients, a fourth ink, clean registration.
three-ink-stencil-print.shot: A handheld follow behind a moving light, then a slow push in, with the plates kicking slightly off register on accents and snapping back on the downbeat. The transition is an overprint: a shape of one ink grows over the whole frame, then shrinks into the next scene's key shape.
three-ink-stencil-print.sound: A late-1960s night groove at a slow, swampy tempo: dry electric bass, brushed kit, bluesy electric guitar and a soft electric piano. Warm, slightly lo-fi tape texture; the mood is hot, tense and simmering.

pop-photo-silkscreen.name: Pop photo silkscreen
pop-photo-silkscreen.still: A 1960s pop-art photo silkscreen on brushed silver paint with a soft sheen. Two plates: a high-contrast black halftone photograph with few mid-tones, its dots on a 45-degree screen, over hand-painted flat colour blocks offset about a hundredth of the frame width with wobbly edges: taxi yellow, skin pink, cream and red, together about a third of the frame; silver fills most of the rest. Uneven squeegee pressure floods dots into blotches in places and drags dry horizontal streaks and pinholes elsewhere, over a faint fabric weave. Repetition is the composition: the same full-length form printed side by side two or three times, slightly overlapping, on empty silver. Avoid: clean even halftone, perfect registration, uniform crispness.
pop-photo-silkscreen.shot: Handheld shake and a short push in on the printed forms, then the camera eases back to a flat frontal view. As it settles, one more copy of the same form prints beside the others, a fresh dry horizontal streak sweeping across it as it lands.
pop-photo-silkscreen.sound: Late-1960s city folk-pop at a loping medium tempo: a harmonica melody over strummed acoustic guitar, upright bass and brushes, with a lonely whistled line. Slightly melancholy, drifting and street-worn.

hand-block-print.name: Hand block-printed cotton
hand-block-print.still: A hand block print on undyed cotton in the Indian tradition. Undyed cotton is the ground, over half the frame and also the skin tone; indigo for cool areas, shade and patterns, about a fifth; madder red borders and clothing; turmeric small motifs; a black key block the outlines. Blocks about an eighth of the frame height are stamped two to four pixels off register; dye bleeds along the weave and fills unevenly, with fine, sparse mud-resist crackle only inside indigo. A flat frieze in a paisley and vine border, scallop rows for waves wherever the scene shows water, figures in profile with kohl-lined eyes. Avoid: vector edges, perfect registration, dense crackle, indigo flooding the frame.
hand-block-print.shot: A slow lateral pan along the frieze, then a push in until the dye soaked into the weave fills the frame. The transition is a motif from the border that turns and becomes the next stamped scene.
hand-block-print.sound: A steady processional bed at walking pace: a tanpura drone, a sitar melody, soft tabla and a bansuri flute line. Earthy, calm and determined, building slowly.

natural-history-copperplate.name: Natural-history specimen plate
natural-history-copperplate.still: A hand-coloured natural-history copperplate. Every object is engraved in warm black-brown line: dense parallel and cross-hatching, thicker in the darks, stipple for soft tones, hatched shadows beneath; where the scene shows sky, it stays bare paper or a few sparse lines. Flat watercolour tints of medium saturation sit inside the lines: paper about half the plate, umber, rust, yellow and grey-violet sharing the rest. Plate layout: the main figure centred as Fig. 1 at about sixty percent of plate height, three to six small numbered detail figures around it, a spaced small-caps title above and a numbered legend below, both in the language of this prompt, a bevelled plate mark and light foxing. Even daylight. Avoid: smooth gradients, garish colour, a tiny vignetted centre.
natural-history-copperplate.shot: Starting from the finished plate, whatever moves does so lightly and sparingly, the engraved lines and tints holding steady, then a slow, even push toward a key detail as if under a loupe. The transition is a tissue guard laid over the plate, or a region burnished away and re-engraved as the next image.
natural-history-copperplate.sound: A cool, sparse chamber piece at a slow tempo: harpsichord and solo cello, with a glass harmonica shimmering above. Quiet, precise and eerie, with long silences between phrases.

art-nouveau-panel.name: Art Nouveau decorative panel
art-nouveau-panel.still: A turn-of-the-century Art Nouveau colour lithograph panel on cream paper. Pastel flats: sage for vines, leaves and drapery, pale gold for halo and ornament, rose for skin and flowers, and muted teal for shade and a tiled mosaic ornament border, each taking roughly a fifth. Brown contours thicken to double width on the shadow side; each flat carries one hard-edged darker shadow tone; litho grain and a soft vignette. The middle third holds the main form before a large halo filled with fine concentric rings, with arched panels either side, whiplash vines and flowers, no empty area over an eighth of the frame, and a band of serif capitals in the language of this prompt at the foot. Avoid: thin clean lines, saturated colour, empty backgrounds.
art-nouveau-panel.shot: Flowers and vines sway gently as the camera pushes slowly in toward the halo, then eases back out to the whole panel. The transition is a whiplash vine growing across the frame and framing the next panel.
art-nouveau-panel.sound: A graceful turn-of-the-century waltz at a slow, swaying tempo: harp arpeggios, strings, flute and a soft celesta, with distant chimes. Elegant, romantic and dreamy.

linen-postcard.name: Linen-texture postcard
linen-postcard.still: A mid-century linen-texture tourist postcard. Ink lands only on the raised threads of a linen-weave card, leaving a fine crosshatch with white specks in the hollows. Saturated, hand-separated colour with airbrushed blends: bright blue for open, cool areas and any sky the scene shows, about a third, grass green and teal another third, pink accents, cream card for the base tone and the border. Four-point star glints on shiny surfaces; registration off one to two pixels. The main form large and side-on, about half the card's height; big navy 3D block letters with white outlines across the top third spell a place name in the language of this prompt, a small scene inside each letter, a red ribbon banner above. Avoid: weave-less gradients, greyish colour, photographic perspective.
linen-postcard.shot: The picture on the card comes alive, what it shows moving gently, while the camera pushes in slowly and then tracks sideways. The transition is the card flipping over to its printed back, or a new card sliding on top.
linen-postcard.sound: Early-1960s easy-listening road music at a relaxed cruising tempo: twangy electric guitar, upright bass, brushed drums and warm piano. Sunny, nostalgic and gently swinging.

street-stencil.name: Spray stencil on brick
street-stencil.still: Street stencil graffiti on an old red-brick wall. Each image is three to five stencils sprayed as flat colour: hard cut edges, soft overspray where a stencil lifted, spray dots, drips and stencil bridges. Brick and cream painted patches fill about half the frame; black and mid grey most of the rest, gold and red as small accents. Brick relief, mortar and rain streaks show through, so paint sinks into the joints. A busy wall: several images side by side, short hand-sprayed slogans in the language of this prompt, old tags and a torn halftone paste-up. Soft raking daylight. Avoid: clean vector edges, paint floating on the brick, too many colours, a dark wall.
street-stencil.shot: The finished stencil holds on the wall while a last mist of spray drifts off it, then the camera cuts to a close-up and tracks sideways along the brick. The transition is a fresh stencil slapped over the frame and sprayed, its lift revealing the next scene.
street-stencil.sound: A tense modern urban beat at a mid tempo: a muted electric guitar riff, deep bass, a dry snare and a low string drone, with spray-can hiss woven into the rhythm. Gritty, wary and pulsing.

rubber-hose.name: 1930s rubber-hose cartoon
rubber-hose.still: An early-1930s cel cartoon, black and white everywhere but the subject. Every figure but the subject is flat pure black and white with one light grey for hard shadows and a gloss streak on the blacks; the subject gets the same flat fills, hard shadows and gloss streak in its own colours; mid-grey backgrounds, never pure black or white, fill most of the frame. Thick-thin ink lines swell on the side away from an upper-left light; living forms get noodle limbs, round shapes, white gloves and pie-cut eyes. Backgrounds keep graphite lines under grey watercolour washes with pooled, granulating edges; film grain, slightly uneven exposure, scratches and dust over all. Only the subject keeps its own colours, while everything else stays in the style's black, white and greys. Stage-like eye-level framing, the subject posed squarely. Avoid: smooth vector lines, figures melting into grey backgrounds, gradients.
rubber-hose.shot: A mostly locked, eye-level stage view where everything bounces on the beat: the subject anticipates, overshoots and settles, squashing on landings and stretching on fast moves, with a small camera jolt on any impact. Camera moves are just a hard cut to a close-up for the reaction or an eased trucking pan alongside the action. Along with what moves, the film grain, scratches and dust jitter over the picture and its exposure flickers faintly. It ends with a black iris closing in on the beat, never a dissolve.
rubber-hose.sound: A 1930s hot dance band at a bouncy medium-fast tempo: stride piano, clarinet, plunger-muted trumpet, smearing trombone, tuba oom-pah, banjo on the off-beats and brushed snare, with xylophone, woodblock and slide whistle for comic accents. A short syncopated theme stops dead before each gag and is heard through a thin, band-limited old optical soundtrack with gentle wow, hiss and crackle. Playful and mischievous; no string pads, no synthesizers.

modernist-cartoon.name: Midcentury modernist cartoon
modernist-cartoon.still: A flat, geometric 1950s limited-animation cartoon on cream paper. Pale aqua and cream paper cover most of the frame; mustard, teal and orange-red appear only as small accents, and greens and slate blues are those colours mixed toward the paper. Uneven warm-black ink lines, sometimes broken, with colour blocks printed slightly off them, all shifted the same way. Forms are overlapping flat cut-out facets, a lit face plus a shadow face one flat step darker; light beams are pale flat wedges; light crayon grain everywhere with a few paper flecks. Poster layout: one big graphic shape, such as a sun disc or a tower, beside the angular, outlined subject. Avoid: gradients, perfect registration, saturated colour everywhere.
modernist-cartoon.shot: The camera is a fixed animation stand, never handheld: a slow push of a few percent or a gentle parallax drift. On top of that, whatever moves does so in limited-animation steps on the beat, jumping between a few held poses instead of moving smoothly. It leaves through a circular iris or a flat colour-block wipe from the side, cut on a beat with no dissolve.
modernist-cartoon.sound: A light West Coast cool-jazz combo at an easy medium swing: flute or muted trumpet, vibraphone chords and glissandi, pizzicato walking bass, brushes, celesta, and bongos or finger snaps. Clean, airy and witty, with short silences that let single accents land; no ragtime, no big band, no strings.

superhero-comic-page.name: 1970s superhero comic page
superhero-comic-page.still: A 1970s four-colour comic-book page printed on aged newsprint. Cyan, magenta, yellow and black flats print as round 45-degree halftone dots; bare paper shows through about a third of the page, heavy blacks take about another third, and the colour plates sit one pixel off register. Heavy tapered brush contours, feathered spot blacks, crackling black energy bubbles, bold block-letter sound effects, hand-lettered balloons and yellow caption boxes, all lettered in the language of this prompt; paper fibre, browned edges, a gutter fold shadow and warm lamp falloff. Laid out in panels with a dominant splash panel for the subject, in exaggerated, forced perspective. Avoid: smooth digital gradients, clean white paper, stiff tube-like machines.
superhero-comic-page.shot: The camera reads the page like a comic: a slow push into the splash panel, then a pan along a strip of panels, each hard cut landing on a beat. As it pushes in, the halftone dots swell into large pop-art dots, and it leaves by a page turn that flips to the next spread.
superhero-comic-page.sound: A punchy 1970s funk-and-brass action cue at an urgent mid-tempo: wah-wah guitar, fat electric bass, tight drums with open hi-hats, stabbing brass and a swelling string synthesizer. Bold, heroic and comic-book bright, with a sharp brass hit at the end of every four-bar phrase.

fashion-illustration.name: 1960s fashion illustration
fashion-illustration.still: A 1960s fashion illustration in fast ink and loose watercolour on white paper. Pink washes lead, with magenta hot spots, rose, a touch of plum and warm grey for secondary shapes; washes cover about two thirds of the frame, the rest bare paper. Quick ink line, thicker at corners, thinner on tight curves, ending in a dry-brush flick; solid black for dark masses and stripes; soft-edged colour pools darken at their drying edges, with directional splatter; settings are only a few lines. A horizontal frieze of elongated forms, the subject repeated as warm-grey wash echoes across the frame, black-and-white pattern over pink. Avoid: even-width outlines, flat digital fills, hard polygon washes, a lone figure on an empty page.
fashion-illustration.shot: A slow, unhurried lateral drift along the frieze, the washes breathing slightly as if still wet. Transitions are graphic masks: a black shape such as a hat brim or a circle lifts or closes to reveal the next frame, or a pink wash bleeds across the paper and carries the picture away.
fashion-illustration.sound: Elegant early-1960s orchestral pop at a lilting medium tempo: pizzicato and bowed strings, harpsichord or celesta, light woodwinds and a soft brushed snare with a gentle waltz-like sway. Chic, airy and playful, like a slow promenade along a runway.

magazine-cover-illustration.name: Mid-century magazine cover painting
magazine-cover-illustration.still: A warm, realist mid-century magazine-cover illustration in oils on fine-grained board. Palette: plaster cream, oak brown, slate, brass and warm ink-brown, with leaf and bottle greens and brick red; oak and ink darks take about a third of the frame, cream and warm mid-tones most of the rest. Forms are blocky planes (lit, shadow, a warm bounce from below) filled with blended strokes that follow the form; dark contours thicken on the shadow side; a warm key light from the upper left throws cool blue-grey shadows; light board grain, a warm varnish vignette. A deep three-quarter or one-point view with period detail, haze and small background storytelling. Avoid: stiff cut-out shapes, cartoon faces, even outlines, muddy colour, empty backgrounds, a masthead, cover lines or any other lettering.
magazine-cover-illustration.shot: One long, smooth push from the whole scene in to the subject, unhurried, the painted forms moving whole with a slight breath or sway. Any cut lands closer than the last and ends on a detail; the shot closes by settling into a printed page with no lettering as the page turns.
magazine-cover-illustration.sound: Warm small-band Americana from the 1930s to the 1950s at a relaxed medium tempo: ragtime-tinged upright piano, clarinet, muted cornet, banjo or acoustic guitar, upright bass and soft brushed drums. Sly, nostalgic and good-humoured, like a sunny small-town afternoon.

airbrush-80s.name: 1980s airbrush illustration
airbrush-80s.still: A 1980s airbrush illustration with a thin technical-drawing overlay. Bright and high-key: mint and cream fill most of the frame, with neon pink and magenta accents and a black-and-white checkerboard on any floor or ground the scene shows; purple and night tones under a fifth; pink carries any sunset. Every shape is a hard-edged mask of smooth sprayed gradient with a fine overspray rim; people get smooth flat skin, few crisp lines, dark hair masses and pink-and-mint rim light; metal and glass get banded pink-and-mint reflections cut by one hard dark line, and cross-star glints. On top: thin cyan callouts, dotted leaders, dashed rings, dimension lines and monospace numbers counting parts of the scene. Centred poster composition. Avoid: striped retro sunsets, UI boxes, soft edges.
airbrush-80s.shot: A slow, glossy push in or pull out while the cyan callouts blink on the beat and their monospace numbers tick. Cross-star glints flare across any metal or glass on the beat, and the shot changes as a hard-edged mask sweeps across the frame like a fresh airbrush stencil.
airbrush-80s.sound: A glossy mid-1980s synth-pop instrumental at a steady mid tempo: analogue polysynth pads, a bright arpeggiated sequence, gated-reverb drums, slap bass and a soft saxophone lead. Cool, sleek and precise, with small blips that tick on each beat.

pixel-16bit.name: 16-bit arcade fighter
pixel-16bit.still: An original 16-bit arcade fighting-game screen, drawn at 320×180, scaled up by whole numbers into crisp nearest-neighbour pixels, faint CRT scanlines. About 32 colours per frame: the scene written here, flattened into a side-on arena, fills most of the screen, a dark purple crowd or backdrop band across the upper third, yellow health bars with a red damage trail along the top. Chunky sprites about 50 pixels tall with one-pixel highlights and dark outlines; a hand-made blocky pixel font for the round timer, a round-number and start-call banner and a combo counter, all in the language of this prompt. Fixed side-on framing, the subject facing a rival across the stage, or a personified obstacle such as a storm. Avoid: real games' characters or logos, anti-aliased or blurry pixels.
pixel-16bit.shot: A locked side-on game camera with no cuts: the subject steps forward, trades blows and lands a hit that sparks, freezes for three or four frames and flashes white, knocking the rival back. The round ends on a blinking knockout call and a winner banner in the language of this prompt, then the screen breaks into a pixel mosaic and wipes away.
pixel-16bit.sound: A driving 16-bit arcade chiptune at a fast tempo: a pulse-wave lead, triangle bass, crunchy noise drums and a wavetable melody with short console-style echo. Tense and pumped-up, with stabbing hits, a rising fanfare and bit-crushed impact accents.

sepia-albumen.name: Sepia albumen panorama
sepia-albumen.still: A gold-toned 1880s albumen photograph built from soft-edged painted shapes. Outside the subject, sepia only: cream highlights cover about half the frame, umber mid-tones about a third, deep brown shadows the rest, darkening into a vignette. Fine hatching, slight lens softness, a faint sideways ghost that grows with motion, blotchy development, silver grain, dust and scratches. Only the subject keeps its own colours, laid on as transparent hand-tinting with a feathered edge, and the rest stays in the style's sepia. Framed as a long, wide print: a pale upper band, a middle band of small repeated elements drawn from the scene, no single large plane. Avoid: hard ink outlines, other colours outside the subject, a flat grey print, a clean digital backdrop.
sepia-albumen.shot: Ease slowly across the long, wide frame with a gentle push in over four to five seconds, the sideways ghosting stretching while the camera moves and settling when it stops. End as the edges of the print slowly darken, as if the sheet is still being toned.
sepia-albumen.sound: A late-19th-century parlour tune for upright piano in a slow, lilting waltz, with a fiddle carrying a plain folk melody and a soft reed organ holding the chords. About 90 beats per minute, dry and a little worn, warm and nostalgic, like a frontier song half remembered.

studio-glamour-bw.name: Glamour-still black and white
studio-glamour-bw.still: Painted like a retouched 1940s soundstage glamour still, in smooth airbrushed tones. Outside the subject, black and white only: deep black covers 30 to 40 percent of the frame, rich mid-greys most of the rest, whites small and glowing; where the scene shows sky, it stays mid-dark. Short lighting leaves a small triangle on the shadowed cheek and two catchlights per eye; slatted, blind-like shadows fall diagonally, light shafts show only in smoke or fog, with diffusion glow, fine grain and a soft vignette. Only the subject keeps its own colours, and the rest stays in the style's black and white, any lamps included. Compose as a soft glamour close-up or a deep, layered view, with smoke or mist drifting through it. Avoid: flat light, an even grey haze, stiff busts.
studio-glamour-bw.shot: A long, smooth glide drifts through the smoke or mist and settles into a slow push toward the brightest highlight, then eases back into the haze. End on a soft iris or a slow fade to black.
studio-glamour-bw.sound: A 1940s soundstage orchestra: lush strings, a muted trumpet and a soft clarinet over brushed drums and slow piano, a romantic ballad at about 70 beats per minute. Warm, slightly hissy mono, smoky and bittersweet, swelling gently toward the end.

halftone-spread.name: Picture-magazine halftone spread
halftone-spread.still: A 1946 picture-magazine spread: a photograph printed as a 45-degree black halftone on coated paper. Outside the subject, off-white paper and grey dots fill most of the frame and solid black about a fifth; a short black headline and caption, in the language of this prompt, sit in a quiet area. Dot spacing about 1/250 of the frame width, slight ink spread, long low-sun shadows, deep focus near and far, a soft gutter crease down the middle. Only the subject keeps its own colours, printed flat from separate spot plates, one for each colour, slightly off register, and the rest stays in the style's black and white. The photo bleeds across both pages, the subject at least a quarter of the frame height and clear of the gutter. Avoid: coarse broken dots, smooth digital gradients.
halftone-spread.shot: Along with what moves, the printed page carries a faint pulse; hold the framing for a beat, then snap-zoom into the halftone until the dots grow huge, or push slowly into one detail. End by pulling back until the photo shrinks into an open magazine lying on a desk, or wipe away with a spreading field of dots; no dissolves.
halftone-spread.sound: A playful, punchy bed built from synths: a tight kick and snare, a bouncy eighth-note bass, a marimba-like pluck carrying the tune and finger snaps, around 110 beats per minute. Crisp and dry with a sly, investigative mood, dropping to near silence for a beat before one final stamp-like hit.

kinescope-tv.name: 1950s tube-TV recording
kinescope-tv.still: A 1950s broadcast recording, black and white everywhere but the subject, playing on a wood-cabinet television with a rounded, bulging tube. The screen fills about 60 percent of the frame, in cool phosphor greys outside the subject, whites a pale cool blue-grey; the rest is a warm, flat-illustrated living room in ochre and wood under a table lamp, cold blue screen light on the walls. On screen: soft detail, about 330 scanlines, halation, ghosting, a faint dark hum bar across the picture, light snow, lifted blacks and grain. Only the subject keeps its own colours, under the same scanlines and ghosting, and the rest of the broadcast stays in the style's black and white. The set is framed squarely in the room, its broadcast a steady mid shot. Avoid: heavy snow, a dull, evenly lit room.
kinescope-tv.shot: Hold on the television in the room for about two seconds, then push through the glass until the broadcast fills the frame with the scanlines still showing. End as the picture rolls once and shrinks to a bright dot, the way an old set switches off.
kinescope-tv.sound: 1950s living-room television music: a small orchestra with warm strings, a gentle clarinet and a soft brushed rhythm in a slow, tender ballad around 80 beats per minute. Thin, boxy mono as if from a small speaker, with a faint hum and tape hiss; shy and hopeful.

hand-tinted-photo.name: Hand-tinted sepia print
hand-tinted-photo.still: A hand-coloured toned silver photograph from about 1900, softly lit from the upper left. Outside the subject, the full sepia range runs from deep brown through warm mid-brown to pale cream, with at least a fifth of the frame at the dark end and mid-tones most of the rest. Soft focus, light halation, grain heaviest in the mid-tones, soft shading; light ageing with a vignette, silvered border darks, small foxing spots, fine scratches and at most one cracked corner. Only the subject keeps its own colours, brushed loosely past its edges as transparent dye that fades in shadow, and the rest stays in the style's sepia. Frontal and documentary, everything still and facing the lens. Avoid: toy-like figures, flat digital fill, low-contrast fog, large mould blotches.
hand-tinted-photo.shot: A slow sideways pan across the frontal scene with the faintest drift inward, as if an eye were moving over an old print. End with the dye wash seeping a little further, then the print yellowing and fading out to its paper edge.
hand-tinted-photo.sound: Turn-of-the-century music: a solo accordion or mandolin with a softly bowed violin, a slow, wistful melody around 70 beats per minute. Sparse and slightly worn, like an early cylinder recording, tender and full of longing for a distant home.

instant-film-album.name: Instant-film family album
instant-film-album.still: Faded 1970s and 80s instant-film snapshots and colour prints in an open family album. Cream pages take about a third of the frame and the photos, which show the subject in the scene written here, the rest; in them blacks lift to a teal grey, highlights roll off to cream, with a mild warm cast and saturation about 60 percent of normal. Fine grain, softness, white instant-film borders, four-frame photo-booth strips, ballpoint captions in the language of this prompt and a faint plastic sheen. Seen from directly above in soft, even light; moving things get a panning-shutter look with the background smeared sideways, still things a shallow depth of field, everything photographed rather than drawn. Avoid: flat cartoon shapes, crisp modern colour, light shafts, saturated prints.
instant-film-album.shot: Start overhead on the open album and push into one photo for about three seconds until it fills the frame, then cut inside it as the moment in the photo comes to life, its faded colour unchanged. End with a gentle pull-back, or with the album page turning to the next spread.
instant-film-album.sound: A warm late-1970s soft-rock bed: clean electric piano, strummed acoustic guitar, a mellow bass and a light drum kit at about 85 beats per minute. Gently saturated tape warmth with a slight wobble, nostalgic and tender, like a home movie of a happy summer.

bw-colour-accent.name: Black and white with one colour
bw-colour-accent.still: Black-and-white motion-picture film everywhere outside the subject, which is the only coloured thing in the frame. Outside the subject, cold neutral greys fill nearly all the frame, a strong S-curve from near-black to near-white, an overcast mid-key with open shadows. Haloed highlights in haze, a soft old lens, coarse silver grain, rare dust and a vignette. Only the subject keeps its own colours, saturated and clear, and the rest stays in the style's black and white, any lamps or fire in the scene included. Long-lens compression, soft out-of-focus shapes in the foreground; the framing looks down from a little height, the subject still large enough to recognise, set apart among any other figures in the scene or alone with open grey space around it. Avoid: sepia or blue toning, grain-free greys, more than one coloured thing.
bw-colour-accent.shot: A slow long-lens push toward the coloured subject, or a steady lateral track alongside it, the subject held in frame, the grain alive and flickering slightly. End on a hard cut, or let the grain thicken as the frame fades to black.
bw-colour-accent.sound: A sparse, mournful chamber piece: a solo violin over low sustained strings and a quiet piano, slow and rubato at about 60 beats per minute. Restrained and grieving, with long silences between phrases and a faint, hopeful lift at the end.

silent-film-bw.name: Polished silent-film black and white
silent-film-bw.still: A modern homage to late-1920s silent film, everything around the subject in clean black and white, 4:3 inside a 16:9 frame with black side bars. Outside the subject, deep blacks take about a third of the frame, soft mid-greys most of the rest, highlights small and glowing; a gentle S-curve and grey halation around lights.
