Fine grain, a slightly uneven exposure, a few specks of dust. Only the subject keeps its own colours, wholly and cleanly, and the rest stays in the style's black and white, lamps and fire included. Give the scene grand, ordered staging like a silent-film set, with a wrought-iron staircase or a gilt proscenium where the place allows; figures mostly in elegant profile. Avoid: heavy scratches, sepia tint, colour bleeding into the greys.
silent-film-bw.shot: The camera stays mostly locked on the opening framing, with at most one slow, motivated push-in and a slight projector flicker throughout. Flash in a title card for a beat: black, with a deco border and spaced capitals in the language of this prompt. Close with an iris, a fade to black or a falling curtain; no dissolves and no modern whip pans.
silent-film-bw.sound: A lone upright piano in the old picture-house tradition, perhaps joined by a violin, with a stride left hand and a lyrical theme. Light, brisk and charming at about 110 beats per minute, over the soft whir and click of a film projector.

daguerreotype.name: Cased silver-plate photograph
daguerreotype.still: An 1850s cased silver-plate photograph. The plate fills about 85 percent of the frame width with a mirror-like surface, inside a beaded brass mat with a round-cornered rectangular opening; velvet and leather show only at the edges. A thin blue-violet to amber tarnish halo rings the opening, with faint polishing swirls, hairline scratches and specks. Only the subject keeps its own colours, as a translucent flat hand-tinted wash with the shading showing through, and the rest stays in the style's mirror-like greyscale from near-black to pale silver. Soft window light from the upper left, the subject posed still before a painted backdrop of the scene. Avoid: sepia, a small plate.
daguerreotype.shot: Push in from the open case to the plate in about a second, then hold one unbroken shot while the mirror-like plate shimmers as the angle shifts, the image flashing briefly to negative and back. Any further movement is slow and small, with no cuts.
daguerreotype.sound: Mid-19th-century parlour music: a solo fiddle playing a slow, plaintive air over a quiet sustained drone, about 60 beats per minute. Bare, intimate and dignified, with a little room echo and long pauses.

neon-snow-night.name: Snowy neon night photograph
neon-snow-night.still: A photographic neon night lit by real tubes: glass, glow, white-hot cores, clips and dark wires. A deep purple-blue night fills about half the frame; pink, cyan, orange and green neon with warm sodium light share the rest. Wet ground fills the lower quarter, signs stretching into long vertical reflections broken by joints or ripples; snow falls and piles at the edges, tinted by the spill; bloom, vignette, fine grain. Place neon where the setting allows, such as shopfronts or a bar; a warm key from a nearby lamp lights the main figure or object, with thin neon rims on both sides and the distance melting into bokeh. Avoid: flat painted neon lettering, dry ground.
neon-snow-night.shot: Two short beats of two to three seconds on one place: the first holds the opening framing with a slow push-in, the second comes from a new angle with a slow push-in, snow drifting through the frame. Pass between them as a sign flickers off and on, or let a neon glow bloom to white and carry the cut. Otherwise the neon glows steadily and never strobes.
neon-snow-night.sound: A modern late-night bed: a slow, hazy synth-pop groove with a warm analogue pad, a soft drum machine, a deep round bass and a twinkling bell motif, around 90 beats per minute. Glossy, slightly melancholic and dreamy, like a cold city night after a party.

stained-glass.name: Backlit stained glass
stained-glass.still: A backlit Gothic stained-glass window filling 80 to 90% of the frame height, neighbouring windows glowing at the edges. The panes picture the subject in the scene written here. Colour by role: cobalt blue for the background and cool areas, about half the window; ruby on the beaded border; gold for highlights; deep greens for any plants and ground; pale amber for skin; black lead throughout. Every shape is a separate piece of cut glass, slightly varied in lightness, with streaks and seed bubbles, joined by thin black lead; faces and folds in fine dark-brown painted line; empty areas cut into small diamond panes. The main figure fills at least half the window's height; bright glass blooms into the leads and coloured light pools on the sill and floor. Avoid: flat fills, random cuts, a dark empty wall around the window.
stained-glass.shot: The camera tilts slowly down the window, pans along a band of lit panes, then follows the coloured shafts down to settle on the light pooled on the stone floor. Scenes change by light alone: a pane wakes as the light reaches it, or the whole window darkens and returns in a new colour; never a dissolve or wipe.
stained-glass.sound: A slow, reverberant piece in the church modes: organ with a soft pedal drone, harp and hand chimes, a recorder line over open fifths. Unhurried and luminous at about 60 beats per minute, with a long bell ring and the faint ring of struck glass in a stone hall.

toy-theatre.name: Paper toy theatre
toy-theatre.still: A nineteenth-century paper toy theatre, everything printed on card. Muted antique hand colouring: deep red and dull gold on the proscenium and drapes, about a third of the frame; the painted scenery behind in greyed browns, greys and cream card for the rest, with small touches of blue; the subject keeps its own clothing and skin colours, softened into the same muted hand colouring. Thin black lithographic outlines, sparse crayon hatching on one side of each piece, and a narrow white scissor margin around every cut-out. Flats stand in parallel flat layers, one behind another with a visible gap between them; candle footlights throw each cut-out's soft, enlarged shadow onto the scenery behind. A gilt proscenium, red drapes and painted spectators in painted audience boxes frame a stage opening most of the frame wide, and the scene written here is what plays on that stage, its places painted on the flats. Avoid: bright vector colour, real 3D depth, soft photographic light, cut-outs without margins.
toy-theatre.shot: A slow push toward the stage with a lateral track across the flats, layers sliding in parallax and footlight shadows flickering; close-ups carry a slight hand tremor. Scenes change the theatre's own way: a new printed flat slides in on its wire, or the curtain drops and rises, and the shot may end by pulling back to the dark room around the little stage.
toy-theatre.sound: A small nineteenth-century parlour band: a slightly out-of-tune upright piano, a fiddle and a penny whistle playing a jaunty music-hall tune in a bouncing two-step at about 110 beats per minute. Light and cheeky with a hint of melancholy, over the soft rattle of cards sliding in their grooves.

rococo-silhouette.name: Candlelit cut-paper silhouettes
rococo-silhouette.still: Eighteenth-century rococo cut-paper silhouettes lit by candlelight. Reds and golds fill most of the frame: gilt relief and red velvet frame the scene like an opera box, solid black profiles stand in front, night blue only where the scene shows sky far back. Each silhouette carries its own cut detail (hair, profile line, lace holes, small objects), a thin pale-gold rim on the side facing the nearest flame and hairline gold lines along the folds of their clothes; warm candle halos, light haze, vignette, fine grain. Signature framing: dark silhouettes in the foreground framing the brightly lit scene far back, cut and lit like a paper-theatre backdrop. Avoid: plain black blobs, copy-pasted profiles, blue walls, blown-out flames.
rococo-silhouette.shot: A slow lateral glide across the paper layers in parallax, then a gentle push toward the lit scene far back while the candles flicker softly. Scenes change with a paper action: a sheet peels away or a page turns to reveal the next layer; no dissolves.
rococo-silhouette.sound: Eighteenth-century chamber music for harpsichord and a small string ensemble, a graceful minuet in triple time at a moderate tempo. Elegant, warm and slightly theatrical, with the soft murmur of a candlelit hall and the faint snip of scissors through paper.

pop-up-book.name: Pop-up book spread
pop-up-book.still: A real pop-up book photographed on a wooden desk. Every element is a flat die-cut card standing on parallel folds in front of an upright backdrop page, printed in transparent watercolour with grainy coloured-pencil hatching; cut edges show a white core and grey board. Clear print colours for the scene's own time of day (cerulean blue, warm sand and fresh greens by day) fill most of the spread, the walnut desk runs along the bottom, and the room behind is a warm blur. Bright window light from the upper left casts soft shadows between the layers; the time of day exists only in the printed picture. Shallow physical depth of field on the main layer; signature framing is a high three-quarter view of the whole open spread. Avoid: solid-looking cards, dark moody rooms, cartoon faces.
pop-up-book.shot: One continuous move from the open book: the camera dips into the spread to the paper figures' eye level with shallow focus, then rises back to a three-quarter view of the whole book. A page turn replaces any cut, old pieces folding flat as new ones spring up; never a video dissolve.
pop-up-book.sound: Whimsical acoustic music for music box, pizzicato strings, clarinet, glockenspiel and toy piano with light brushes, at about 100 beats per minute. Gentle and storybook-warm, over crisp paper snaps, page swishes and a quiet room tone.

roman-mosaic.name: Ancient stone floor mosaic
roman-mosaic.still: An ancient floor mosaic of small square stone and glass tesserae, each about 1/150 of frame width. Muted warm stone fills the frame: warm marble for broad light areas, pale grey-blue stone for cool areas and shade, burnt gold, umber and terracotta for figures and objects, one small accent of imperial-purple glass. Two or three courses of stones follow every outline, flat areas run in straight rows, and figures are outlined by one course of dark stones; each tessera is slightly irregular, lit from the upper left and set in dark 1 to 2 px grout, with gold-leaf glass glinting at light sources. Figures stand frontal and a little stiff; the scene behind them is laid in finer, fainter stones. Avoid: a neat grid that reads as pixel art, oversized tiles, smooth gradients, bright grout.
roman-mosaic.shot: Short, slow pushes and pulls only. The stones keep their places and the picture moves across them; where the picture has them, small details such as a gesture, swaying plants or a shaft of light can stir as well. To change scene, tesserae flip or slide row by row into the next picture, the gold glass catching the light.
roman-mosaic.sound: Music of the ancient Mediterranean: lyre and plucked kithara over a frame drum, a double-reed pipe melody and a low drone, at a steady walking pace near 80 beats per minute. Stately, sun-warmed and austere, in the dry acoustic of an open courtyard.

cut-paper-titles.name: Black-and-white line titles
cut-paper-titles.still: A mid-century title-sequence style built from lines: everything outside the subject is black and white with one warm accent. Outside the subject, flat greys in four or five even steps from near-black to warm off-white cover the frame, light to mid grey dominating; outside the subject, orange-red is the only warm colour, kept small, and all light stays white. Thin white construction lines and a dark outline about 1/600 of frame width around every shape; flat fills, light grain, soft vignette. Only the subject keeps its own colours, and everything else stays in the black-and-white greys and the one orange-red accent. Strict one-point perspective with a centred vanishing point, identical elements (posts, lamps, windows, desks) repeating into depth. Avoid: sketchy lines, gradients, colour leaks outside the subject, skewed perspective, unfilled wireframe.
cut-paper-titles.shot: Hold the finished perspective for a beat while lights blink along the repeated rows, then the camera crash-pushes toward the centre on a hard beat. A hard cut to a straight-down view turns the repeated rows into a flat pattern; transitions are graphic match cuts and lines drawing themselves, never dissolves.
cut-paper-titles.sound: A 1960s big-band cue: stacked staccato trumpet and trombone stabs, a walking upright bass, brushed drums with bongos, vibraphone and a twangy guitar soaked in spring reverb, in a minor key at about 130 beats per minute. Sharp, cool and suspenseful, with stop-time breaks of total silence between the stabs.

red-black-stage.name: Red-and-black jazz stage
red-black-stage.still: Whatever the scene, it is staged and lit like a stage-musical number: the setting sinks to black, with about 40% of the frame glowing signal red: a row of dark barred openings, each backlit red through haze and falling off to black, red drapes, hard-edged spotlights. Smaller accents: one big neon shape in orange-red with a white-hot core, marquee bulbs along the bottom edge of the frame, a glossy black ground reflecting them. Dancers are full-bodied black silhouettes with costume shapes and a 2 to 3 px red rim; sequins and white gloves catch the light. The central figure stands in a warm-white follow spot, the one fully lit figure in the picture. Avoid: flat even fills, extra colours, rimless silhouettes.
red-black-stage.shot: Movement lands on a jazz beat: the lit openings flicker on the beat, a crash zoom of a few frames punches in on a drum hit, and the camera pushes in to end in the follow spot. Scenes change by light: a spotlight cuts to black and another bangs on, never a crossfade.
red-black-stage.sound: A brassy 1920s vaudeville jazz number: muted trumpet, growling trombone, clarinet, honky-tonk piano, upright bass and a snare with rim shots and cymbal chokes, at a slinky medium swing around 120 beats per minute. Sly, sultry and theatrical, building to a punchy final hit.

manga-impact.name: Manga impact frame
manga-impact.accent: The accent is a manga impact frame: for two or three frames the whole picture turns into a hand-inked comic panel in one line style only, thick black ink outlines on flat white with the colour gone, a burst of speed lines radiating from the point of contact.

white-flash.name: White flash
white-flash.accent: The accent is a white flash: for two or three frames the whole frame flashes bright white outward from the point of contact, the two figures left as crisp dark outlines against the white.

negative-flash.name: Negative flash
negative-flash.accent: The accent is a negative flash: for two or three frames every colour in the frame inverts to its photographic negative, light turned dark and dark turned light, every shape unchanged.

black-flash.name: Black flash
black-flash.accent: The accent is a black flash: for two or three frames the frame drops to black, only the two figures and the point of contact picked out by a thin bright rim of light.
